title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics + schema mapping + tool message formatting
author: Ava Chen
description:
Context: the OpenAI-compat layer has had partial support for function/tool calling, but behavior diverged from OpenAI semantics around tool_choice decisions, schema-to-tool mapping for ambiguous inputs, and how tool-generated messages should be represented in the compat response stream. This PR unifies semantics with OpenAI where possible and documents remaining incompatibilities.

What this PR does: implements explicit tool_choice semantics in the compat layer (first-party fallback and categorical choice), improves tool schema mapping for overlapping schemas (preference by explicit tool id > shape specificity > registration order), and normalizes tool message formatting so that tool outputs are surfaced as assistant-typed messages with metadata (tool name, tool_id, raw_payload). Adds unit + integration tests and updates compat docs.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement tool_choice enum handling and surface in responses
- [x] Schema matching algorithm with deterministic tie-breaker
- [x] Tool message formatting changes and streaming compatibility tests
- [x] Add regression tests for previous failures (see ENG-4217)
- [x] Update API docs and examples in redwood-docs
- [x] Add changelog entry

Motivation: customers using the OpenAI-compatible API expect deterministic tool selection and consistent message framing across streaming and non-streaming responses. Mismatches caused regressions for a few downstream SDKs and led to loss of structured metadata when a tool produced multi-part messages.

Compatibility notes: We strive for parity but keep two intentional deviations: 1) when a tool returns an extremely large raw payload (>4MB) we truncate metadata in-stream and provide a full artifact link in the final response (private deployment safety guard); 2) for on-prem private installers without explicit tool registration order, we fall back to alphabetical tie-breaker (documented). Both are called out in the release notes.

Related: Linear ENG-4217, ENG-4330. Jira SUP-982 for customer reproduction case.

review_comments: Diego Morales (reviewer): Can we add a perf note? The schema matcher now runs N^2 comparisons in the worst case. Suggest adding a short-circuit for exact id matches.
Ava Chen (author): Added short-circuit and a unit test to confirm O(N) path when tool_id present. Benchmarks included in PR show negligible end-to-end latency impact.
Priya Nair (reviewer): The streaming examples in docs should show both chunked tool messages and the final assistant envelope. Also confirm what SDKs need to change.
Ava Chen: Updated docs and added a compatibility shim in python/ts SDKs that normalizes the assistant message envelope to SDK-specific friendly objects.
Maria Gomez (approver): Verified integration tests against the compat harness. CI had a flaky test that I reran. Approving pending changelog entry review.
CI Bot: pipeline passed on rerun (unit, integration, lint). Release note approved by docs.
Release Manager: Merged via squash after changelog confirmation.
release_notes: OpenAI-compat: deterministic tool_choice semantics, improved schema mapping tie-breakers, and normalized tool message formatting for streaming and non-streaming responses. Note: large tool payload truncation behavior and alphabetical tie-breaker for some private installs are intentional deviations. See redwood-docs/openai/tool-calling.md for details.
